gaps.sentence: I have no idea where he is — he ___ have gone to the gym, or maybe to the pool.
gaps.hint: an uncertain guess about the past
gaps.explanation: 'Might have' expresses an uncertain guess about the past: might have gone.

gaps.sentence: The fire spread quickly, but everyone ___ escape.
gaps.hint: one specific achievement in the past
gaps.explanation: For one specific past achievement, 'was able to' or 'managed to' is used, not 'could': was able to escape.

gaps.sentence: It is the only blue house on the street, so you ___ miss it.
gaps.explanation: 'You can't miss it' is an idiom meaning it is impossible not to find: can't.

gaps.sentence: If you want a refund, you ___ keep the receipt — no receipt, no refund.
gaps.hint: a necessity that applies in the future
gaps.explanation: Future necessity uses 'will have to': will have to keep.

gaps.sentence: I didn't ___ to like coffee, but now I drink it every day.
gaps.hint: negative of used to, spelled use
gaps.explanation: In the negative, 'used to' becomes 'didn't use to': use.

gaps.sentence: In this lab, food and drink ___ be brought past the reception area.
gaps.explanation: Written prohibitions use 'must not': must not be brought.

gaps.sentence: Candidates ___ switch off their phones before the exam begins.
Do I ___ to bring my own towel, or is one provided?
gaps.hint: a question about necessity with do
gaps.explanation: Questions about necessity use 'do ... have to': have to bring.
